text:
eli: heads-up — seeing a big prefix cache warmup / hit-rate regression in prod after the kernel rollout last night. overall hit-rate for short prompts dropped from ~78% -> ~22% on mixtral-8x-int8 pools.

sam: link? which pool + time window?

eli: https://console.redwood/perf/dashboards/prefix-cache?range=3h&pool=pool-3 — spike starts right after the flash-attn-v2 roll at ~2026-03-17T03:14Z. first-token latency increased ~18ms for cached prefixes, warmup rate (first 30m) basically evaporated.

rachel: curious if key canonicalization changed. did the compile add any metadata to the model digest used in cache key? any change in quant profile id?

eli: digging through logs — the cache key formula we use is: sha1(prompt_id || model_digest || quant_profile_id). Quick grep shows model_digest now includes a build_id field in the runtime artifact manifest after the new compile step.

sam: whoa. that would make every previously cached key invalid whenever we bump the compiler build id. can you paste the manifest diff?

eli: small excerpt:
```
- model_digest: "sha256:abcd...:weights-v1"
+ model_digest: "sha256:abcd...:weights-v1|build:2026-03-17T03:10:12"
```
so same weights hash but extra build tag appended. keys diverge.

perf-bot: deploy-bot rolled flash-attn-v2 -> backend pool-3 at 2026-03-17T03:14:12Z (deploy id d-4109).

rachel: that aligns. root cause looks like we accidentally started baking ephemeral build metadata into the canonical model id used for cache keying. fix should be removing build_id from the digest used for prefix cache keys (keep only weights+arch+quant_profile).

eli: agree. quick mitigation — can we canary revert kernel on a subset of pool-3 to measure hit-rate reconstitution?

sam: started a canary: pool-3-canary with kernel=flash-attn-v1 (legacy) and same quant profile. initial observations: within 30m the canary hit-rate climbed back to ~71% and first-token latency dropped ~15ms.

rachel: nice — that confirms new kernel itself didn't change semantics, it was the compile pipeline mutation of model_digest. action items: 1) revert build_id inclusion in cache key (PR), 2) add unit tests to ensure digest normalization (strip ephemeral tags), 3) add synthetic warmup test to CI that validates hit-rate for short prompt distributions after compile.

eli: opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/788 (remove build tag from model digest used for cache key). also adding a migration to normalize existing in-memory keys for dedicated pools for ~1 hour to avoid cold start for big customers.

sam: ops note — keeping canary on for 1h, will then route 20% traffic if stable and coordinate a staged rollout. I'll also add a smoke check to alert if hit-rate < 50% for 15m.

rachel: long-term we should change the model artifact schema so build_id is separate and never part of canonical model id. also add a lint that prevents CI from injecting ephemeral fields into digest.

eli: +1. also logging: add a metric for "model_digest_version_mismatch" so we can detect these classes of regressions earlier.

sam: confirmed: canary still at 69% after 45m, will escalate to 20% if no regressions. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

rachel: PR review coming, adding tests.

eli: will follow up with postmortem notes and ETA for full rollout.

sam: fine to close this thread once PR merged and 20% rollout passes.

deploy-bot: note: automated rollback available until 2026-03-17T06:00Z.
